correctness.rationale: Explicit exact proof: graph-Laplacian bound yields a degree-one diffeomorphism and strict Lyapunov descent; the closed triangle x,y in [0,pi], x+y>=pi is forward invariant because sin y<=pi-y<=x and sin x<=pi-x<=y. The two saddle unstable eigendirections have ratios (a+b-E)/b<1 and (a+b+E)/b>1 in their respective positive corner coordinates, whereas stable directions lie outside the triangle; reflection controls the other branch. Hence no saddle connections, and source/sink intersections transverse. At h>=1/Lambda the Jacobian has an exact zero multiplier at cos t=-1/(hLambda). Numerical checks sample but do not prove the universal claim.

value.rationale: The precise structural question is whether strong independent edge imbalance destroys Morse–Smale transversality while preserving the known global Lyapunov behavior. This result answers it uniformly for the minimal nontrivial weighted path and extends the explicit sharp step criterion beyond the known weight-concavity cone; other trees show that sink attraction alone does not guarantee the answer.
